name: v7-learnability
note: V7 diagnostic, not a candidate. Evidence: no V6 or V7 model writes the programs it was trained on: the V6 curriculum model D (72 steps, each v1 program seen ~5 times) passes 1/17 of its own trained programs (code loss 0.39 nats/token), P1 0/17, round 54 0/17; new constants of trained families: D 3/22, P1 1/22, round 54 1/22. Round 54's v5 functions were trained hundreds of times. Question: with the same 24-step budget spent on few programs (the 36 trained programs of the 12 curriculum families parameterised by a constant, 16 write examples per name, ~27 exposures per behaviour), (1) does the model learn them to generation level, (2) does it then write new constants of those families (family_new, never trained), (3) does anything reach the neighbour set? Recipe identical to v7-pairs P1 (seed 1301, 24 steps, lr 1.5e-5, top 24 layers, final_bf16); only the data differs. A small legacy share (1 write per basics concept, 50 replay rows) keeps the answer format.
decision: Diagnostic: not compared with round 54 for adoption. Read: pass on the trained k-family programs (memorization), on family_new (within-family generalization) and on the neighbour set's original prompts (transfer), each against round 54 and D; dev + unseen-v1 for forgetting.
